Everything passed, and your Pi is fully set up.

**What the results mean:**

- **The code builds on Linux.** It compiled with `-Werror` using the Pi's gcc, which is the compiler the graders will use, and all **15 tests passed**.
- **valgrind found nothing: 0 errors, no leaks.** This was the first real valgrind run, since valgrind doesn't work on your Mac. It's the same tool whose findings would cap a component at 50%.
- **The "1 alloc, 1 free, 1,024 bytes" isn't our code.** It's the buffer `printf` sets up for screen output, and it gets freed when the program exits.
- **valgrind also checks for reading memory that was never set.** That's why `record_init` zeroes the whole record first. Without that, any bytes that never got a value would be fed into the checksum, and valgrind would flag it.

To be clear about one thing: the `_POSIX_C_SOURCE` fix from Step 0 still hasn't really been tested. Nothing in Steps 0–2 calls `fsync` or the other functions it's for. That gets tested for real in Step 3, when the storage writer starts using them.

153	## 5. System architecture
154	
155	```
156	                 ZENITH (open sky)
157	    ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
158	    │ TSL2591          MLX90614   │   BME280 (shaded, vented)
159	    │ (acrylic window) (LDPE film │   DS3231 (inside, warm)
160	    │                  + hood)    │
161	    └──────────────┬──────────────┘
162	                   │ I2C bus (3.3 V, ~50 kHz — see §Wiring)
163	═══════════════════╪════════════════════════════ kernel / user boundary
164	        Linux i2c-dev  (serializes bus transactions)
165	                   │
166	   ┌───────────────┼────────────────┬──────────────────┐
167	   │               │                │                  │
168	┌──▼────────┐ ┌────▼──────┐ ┌───────▼─────┐            │
169	│ skyd      │ │ cloudd    │ │ envd        │  one process per sensor
170	│ TSL2591   │ │ MLX90614  │ │ BME280+RTC  │  (mechanism E: isolation)
171	│ ~0.2 Hz   │ │ ~1 Hz     │ │ ~0.1 Hz     │
172	└──┬────────┘ └────┬──────┘ └───────┬─────┘            │
173	   │ SHM ring + sem or UDS          │                  │
174	   └───────────────┼────────────────┘                  │
175	                   │                                    │
176	            ┌──────▼──────────────────────┐             │
177	            │ fusiond (the hub)           │             │
178	            │  · feature extraction       │             │
179	            │  · sun/moon ephemeris (ours)│             │
180	            │  · veto-gate classifier     │             │
181	            │  · state machine + hysteresis│            │
182	            └──────┬──────────────────┬───┘             │
183	                   │                  │                 │
184	          ┌────────▼───────┐  ┌───────▼────────┐        │
185	          │ stored (D)     │  │ LAN/CLI iface  │        │
186	          │ append-only    │  │ dsq query ...  │        │
187	          │ CRC'd records  │  └────────────────┘        │
188	          │ segments+rollup│                            │
189	          └────────────────┘                            │
190	                                                        │
191	            ┌───────────────────────────────────────────▼──┐
192	            │ dskyd — supervisor (E)                       │
193	            │ fork/exec, exponential backoff, DEAD state,  │
194	            │ hourly heartbeat, restart-storm suppression  │
195	            └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
196	```
197	
198	### CHALLENGE 5: all three sensors share one I2C bus — say so, don't hide it
199	
200	Three separate processes hammering one I2C bus is a genuine design problem, not a free lunch. The
201	Linux I2C subsystem serializes transactions, so you will not get corruption — but you *will* get
202	jitter in sample timing and head-of-line blocking when one sensor is slow. This is an honest
203	tradeoff to state in the design doc and **measure** in the evaluation:
204	
205	- Report per-sensor sample-interval jitter with 1 vs. 3 processes contending.
206	- If jitter proves unacceptable, the fallback is a single `i2cd` broker process owning the bus,
207	  with the three sensor daemons as clients. **Decide this in the design doc, not in week 11.**
208	
209	Do not pretend process isolation is costless. Measuring the cost is worth more than hiding it.
210	
211	---
212	
213	## 6. Sensor-fusion design
214	
215	### The core insight — this is your best paragraph, put it in the memo
216	
217	**A brightness sensor alone is not merely imprecise; it is wrong in a specific, demonstrable,
218	reproducible way.**
219	
220	| Sky brightness | ΔT (ambient − sky) | Reality | A light meter alone says |
221	|---|---|---|---|
222	| Dark | Large (clear) | **Excellent night** | "dark, great" ✅ |
223	| Bright | Large (clear) | Clear but moonlit — planets/doubles yes, deep-sky no | "bright, bad" ❌ *wrong* |
224	| Bright | Small (overcast) | Overcast over a city; cloud reflecting streetlight | "bright, bad" ✅ |
225	| **Dark** | **Small (overcast)** | **Overcast at a dark site — useless** | **"dark, great"** ❌ **catastrophically wrong** |
226	
227	That last row is the whole justification for the second sensor. At a rural dark site an overcast
228	sky is genuinely *darker* than a clear one, because there is no light to reflect. A single-sensor
229	meter confidently recommends the worst possible night. The IR channel catches it, and no
230	if-statement on brightness can.
231	
232	### Features (rolling windows, all locally computed)
233	
234	| Feature | Window | What it discriminates |
235	|---|---|---|
236	| `sky_mag` — brightness, calibrated to relative mag/arcsec² | 1 min | darkness level |
237	| `sky_sigma` — rolling std-dev of brightness | 10–30 min | **passing cloud causes variability, not just a level shift** |
238	| `dT = T_amb − T_sky` | 1 min | cloud cover |
239	| `dT_corr = dT + f(RH, T_amb)` — humidity-corrected | 1 min | cloud cover, honestly |
240	| `dT_sigma` | 10–30 min | broken/scattered cloud oscillates |
241	| `dewpoint_margin = T_amb − T_dew` | 5 min | dew risk on optics **and on our own sensor window** |
242	| `dP/dt` — pressure trend | 3 h | front approaching |
243	| `sun_alt`, `moon_alt`, `moon_phase` | computed | see below |
244	
245	`f(RH, T)` must be **fitted from your own logged data**, not guessed. Collect clear humid nights
246	and clear dry nights and regress. If you cannot separate them, say so and narrow the claim.
247	
248	### The sophistication multiplier: local sun/moon ephemeris
249	
250	Implement solar and lunar position from the RTC plus a hardcoded latitude/longitude, in C, from
251	standard astronomical algorithms. This is **pure local computation — no API, no network** — and it
252	transforms the product:
253	
254	1. **Gating.** Astronomical darkness is `sun_alt < −18°`. Without this the device confidently
255	   grades a bright evening twilight as "POOR conditions" when the correct answer is "not dark yet."
256	2. **Attribution.** Knowing moon altitude and phase lets you predict the *expected* moonlight
257	   contribution and therefore attribute measured brightness to a cause: moon, light pollution, or
258	   cloud-scattered glow. "Bright because the moon is up and 87% illuminated" is a genuine
259	   explanation; "bright" is not.
260	3. **Defensibility.** It is math you wrote and can derive at the whiteboard, which is exactly what
261	   the individual defense rewards.
262	
263	This is the single highest-leverage component in the design. It is also self-contained and
264	testable offline against published almanac values — a perfect unit-test target.
265	
266	### Classifier: veto gates, not a weighted sum
267	
268	**CHALLENGE 6: do not use a weighted score.** A weighted sum is hard to explain, hard to defend
269	line-by-line, and produces absurd outputs (enough darkness "outvoting" solid overcast). Use a
270	**veto hierarchy**, which is more explainable and trivially traceable:
271	
272	```
273	1. NOT_DARK      if sun_alt > -18°                         → state: DAYLIGHT / TWILIGHT
274	2. UNKNOWN       if any required sensor DEAD or window has
275	                 < X% expected samples or baseline immature
276	3. POOR  (veto)  if dT_corr < cloud_overcast_threshold      → "overcast"
277	4. POOR  (veto)  if dewpoint_margin < 1 °C AND dT collapsed → "likely dew on window, not sky"
278	5. MARGINAL      if dT_sigma high                           → "broken cloud"
279	   MARGINAL      if sky_sigma high                          → "unstable brightness"
280	   MARGINAL      if moon_alt > 0 AND phase > 0.5            → "moonlight limits deep-sky"
281	6. GOOD          if none of the above fired AND sky_mag
282	                 within the top band of the site baseline
283	```
284	
285	Every rule that fires contributes its reason string. **Explainability is not a feature bolted on;
286	it is a side effect of the architecture.** That is the right way to build it and a good thing to
287	say out loud at the defense.
288	
289	---
290	
291	## 7. State machine
292	
293	States: `BOOT` → `DAYLIGHT` / `TWILIGHT` / `UNKNOWN` / `POOR` / `MARGINAL` / `GOOD`, plus
294	`DEGRADED` (running with a dead sensor) and `FAULT`.
295	
296	Transition discipline:
297	- **Minimum dwell time** per state (e.g. 10 min) — prevents flapping.
298	- **Asymmetric hysteresis.** Promoting toward GOOD requires N consecutive qualifying windows;
299	  demoting requires fewer. Justify the asymmetry explicitly: a false GOOD sends someone outside
300	  or on a 40-minute drive for nothing, which is the error that gets the device unplugged. Spec
301	  Seed 1 makes the same point — *"a monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged."*
302	- **Every transition is logged** with the rule that caused it and the feature values at the time.
303	  The transition log is the artifact you will read from at the demo when asked "why did it say
304	  that at 1 a.m.?"
305	
306	---
307	
308	## 8. Data model
309	
310	Fixed-width binary records — fixed width matters because it makes torn-write detection and
311	recovery-by-truncation simple.
312	
313	```c
314	/* 48 bytes, explicitly padded, little-endian, version-tagged */
315	struct dsm_record {
316	    uint64_t t_mono_ns;   /* CLOCK_MONOTONIC — interval math          */
317	    uint64_t t_real_ns;   /* CLOCK_REALTIME  — wall clock labelling   */
318	    uint16_t schema_ver;
319	    uint16_t source_id;   /* which daemon produced this               */
320	    uint16_t kind;        /* SAMPLE | FEATURE | STATE | HEARTBEAT | FAULT */
321	    uint16_t flags;       /* VALID | STALE | SYNTHETIC | CALIBRATING  */
322	    int32_t  v[4];        /* fixed-point payload, scale per kind      */
323	    uint32_t seq;         /* per-source sequence — proves no gaps     */
324	    uint32_t crc32;       /* over all preceding bytes                 */
325	};
326	```
327	
328	Design notes worth defending:
329	- **`seq` per source** gives you drop accounting for free: a gap in sequence numbers is provable
330	  data loss, and "zero gaps across 48 hours" is a measurable claim.
331	- **`flags` carries `SYNTHETIC`.** Spec §5 makes this absolute: replayed or synthesized data must
332	  be labeled *everywhere it appears*. Putting it in the record format means you cannot forget.
333	- **Fixed-point, not float.** Deterministic across platforms and trivially CRC-able.
334	
335	---
336	
337	## 9. Storage architecture (mechanism D)
338	
339	```
340	data/
341	  seg-000001.dsm      append-only segment, rotated at 8 MB or at local noon
342	  seg-000002.dsm
343	  index/2026-10-14.rollup    per-night summary written after the night closes
344	  MANIFEST                   segment list + validated-length watermark
345	```
346	
347	- **Superblock** per segment: magic, schema version, creation time, site lat/long.
348	- **Write batching:** accumulate records in an in-memory buffer, `write()` in one syscall.
349	- **fsync policy:** `fsync()` every N seconds and on segment rotation. **N is a tunable you will
350	  experiment on** (§13) — the tradeoff is data-loss window vs. write amplification vs. SD card
351	  wear. Measuring that curve is real systems work.
352	- **Recovery:** on startup, read `MANIFEST` watermark, scan forward validating CRCs, truncate at
353	  the first invalid record, log the truncation. A torn final record is expected and normal, not an
354	  error condition.
355	- **Rollups:** after each night, compute per-night summaries (min/median sky_mag, minutes in each
356	  state, cloud fraction) into a compact index so queries over weeks do not rescan raw segments.
357	- **Retention:** raw segments age out at a documented horizon; rollups are kept indefinitely.
358	  Monitor free space and **refuse to write while logging loudly** rather than filling the card.
359	
360	The crash-consistency story is the deliverable here, and it is testable by literally pulling the
361	plug — repeatedly, and counting (§13).
362	
363	---
364	
365	## 10. Process architecture & mechanism selection
366	
367	### CHALLENGE 7: pick D + E. Do not pick C or F.
368	
369	| Mechanism | Fit | Verdict |
370	|---|---|---|
371	| **D** custom crash-consistent storage | Weeks of nightly baseline must survive power cuts; SD wear is real; retrospective queries are a core feature | **Take it.** Strongly justified by the problem. |
372	| **E** multiprocess + IPC + supervisor | A silently dead sky monitor is this product's nightmare scenario; sensor isolation is a requirement, not garnish | **Take it.** Strongly justified. |
373	| **A** kernel char driver | Could expose the TSL2591 or MLX90614 via `/dev`. Best resume line in the menu. | **Stretch.** Start it only if M3 lands early. Keep the userspace path as fallback. |
374	| **B** interrupt vs. polling | Only honest if you switch to the TSL237 pulse-output sensor. The TSL2591's INT pin on a slowly-varying signal is a weak comparison. | **Only with TSL237.** Don't fake it. |
375	| **C** real-time scheduling | There is no hard deadline in "is the sky dark." Sky brightness changes over minutes. | **Reject.** Forcing `SCHED_FIFO` here is contrived and the defense will find it. |
376	| **F** no-drop high-rate pipeline | Sampling at 0.1–1 Hz. A "no-drop high-rate pipeline" for a 1 Hz signal is transparently padded. | **Reject.** |
377	
378	Being able to say *"we considered C and F and rejected them because our sample rates don't justify
379	them"* is a **stronger** answer at the defense than bolting them on. Judgment is what is being
380	graded.
381	
382	### Processes
383	
384	| Process | Job | Why separate |
385	|---|---|---|
386	| `dskyd` | supervisor: fork/exec children, backoff, heartbeat, DEAD marking | must outlive every failure |
387	| `skyd` | TSL2591 sampling, ~0.2 Hz | an I2C hang here must not kill cloud sensing |
388	| `cloudd` | MLX90614 sampling, ~1 Hz | the most finicky sensor — isolate it |
389	| `envd` | BME280 + RTC, ~0.1 Hz | slow, low risk |
390	| `fusiond` | features, ephemeris, classifier, state machine | the brain; restartable from stored state |
391	| `stored` | storage layer owner | single writer — avoids multi-writer corruption entirely |
392	| `dsq` | query CLI (short-lived) | read-only |
393	
394	**Single-writer storage is a deliberate choice:** exactly one process may write segments, which
395	eliminates a whole class of concurrency bugs by construction rather than by locking.
396	
397	---
398	
399	## 11. IPC design
400	
401	- **Sensor → hub: POSIX shared-memory ring buffer + semaphore**, one ring per sensor daemon,
402	  single-producer/single-consumer. Cheap, bounded, and lets the hub detect overrun explicitly
403	  rather than silently. Per-record `seq` makes any drop provable.
404	- **Hub → storage: Unix domain socket** (`SOCK_SEQPACKET`). Message-oriented, backpressure comes
405	  free from the socket buffer, and the fd dying is an immediate, unambiguous signal that the
406	  storage process is gone.
407	- **CLI → hub: Unix domain socket** with a small request/response protocol for live state.
408	- **Supervisor → children: signals + a pipe-based liveness channel.** Each child holds the write
409	  end of a pipe; the supervisor sees EOF the instant the child dies, without polling. This is a
410	  clean, classic pattern and a good thing to be able to explain.
411	
412	Deliberately using **two different IPC mechanisms** is defensible: the sensor path is high-frequency
413	and fixed-size (shared memory wins), the storage path needs framing and backpressure (sockets win).
414	Be ready to justify that at the defense rather than saying "we used both to tick a box."

## 5. System architecture

```
                 ZENITH (open sky)
    ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
    │ TSL2591          MLX90614   │   BME280 (shaded, vented)
    │ (acrylic window) (LDPE film │   DS3231 (inside, warm)
    │                  + hood)    │
    └──────────────┬──────────────┘
                   │ I2C bus (3.3 V, ~50 kHz — see §Wiring)
═══════════════════╪════════════════════════════ kernel / user boundary
        Linux i2c-dev  (serializes bus transactions)
                   │
   ┌───────────────┼────────────────┬──────────────────┐
   │               │                │                  │
┌──▼────────┐ ┌────▼──────┐ ┌───────▼─────┐            │
│ skyd      │ │ cloudd    │ │ envd        │  one process per sensor
│ TSL2591   │ │ MLX90614  │ │ BME280+RTC  │  (mechanism E: isolation)
│ ~0.2 Hz   │ │ ~1 Hz     │ │ ~0.1 Hz     │
└──┬────────┘ └────┬──────┘ └───────┬─────┘            │
   │ SHM ring + sem or UDS          │                  │
   └───────────────┼────────────────┘                  │
                   │                                    │
            ┌──────▼──────────────────────┐             │
            │ fusiond (the hub)           │             │
            │  · feature extraction       │             │
            │  · sun/moon ephemeris (ours)│             │
            │  · veto-gate classifier     │             │
            │  · state machine + hysteresis│            │
            └──────┬──────────────────┬───┘             │
                   │                  │                 │
          ┌────────▼───────┐  ┌───────▼────────┐        │
          │ stored (D)     │  │ LAN/CLI iface  │        │
          │ append-only    │  │ dsq query ...  │        │
          │ CRC'd records  │  └────────────────┘        │
          │ segments+rollup│                            │
          └────────────────┘                            │
                                                        │
            ┌───────────────────────────────────────────▼──┐
            │ dskyd — supervisor (E)                       │
            │ fork/exec, exponential backoff, DEAD state,  │
            │ hourly heartbeat, restart-storm suppression  │
            └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### CHALLENGE 5: all three sensors share one I2C bus — say so, don't hide it

Three separate processes hammering one I2C bus is a genuine design problem, not a free lunch. The
Linux I2C subsystem serializes transactions, so you will not get corruption — but you *will* get
jitter in sample timing and head-of-line blocking when one sensor is slow. This is an honest
tradeoff to state in the design doc and **measure** in the evaluation:

- Report per-sensor sample-interval jitter with 1 vs. 3 processes contending.
- If jitter proves unacceptable, the fallback is a single `i2cd` broker process owning the bus,
  with the three sensor daemons as clients. **Decide this in the design doc, not in week 11.**

Do not pretend process isolation is costless. Measuring the cost is worth more than hiding it.

---

## 6. Sensor-fusion design

### The core insight — this is your best paragraph, put it in the memo

**A brightness sensor alone is not merely imprecise; it is wrong in a specific, demonstrable,
reproducible way.**

| Sky brightness | ΔT (ambient − sky) | Reality | A light meter alone says |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dark | Large (clear) | **Excellent night** | "dark, great" ✅ |
| Bright | Large (clear) | Clear but moonlit — planets/doubles yes, deep-sky no | "bright, bad" ❌ *wrong* |
| Bright | Small (overcast) | Overcast over a city; cloud reflecting streetlight | "bright, bad" ✅ |
| **Dark** | **Small (overcast)** | **Overcast at a dark site — useless** | **"dark, great"** ❌ **catastrophically wrong** |

That last row is the whole justification for the second sensor. At a rural dark site an overcast
sky is genuinely *darker* than a clear one, because there is no light to reflect. A single-sensor
meter confidently recommends the worst possible night. The IR channel catches it, and no
if-statement on brightness can.

### Features (rolling windows, all locally computed)

| Feature | Window | What it discriminates |
|---|---|---|
| `sky_mag` — brightness, calibrated to relative mag/arcsec² | 1 min | darkness level |
| `sky_sigma` — rolling std-dev of brightness | 10–30 min | **passing cloud causes variability, not just a level shift** |
| `dT = T_amb − T_sky` | 1 min | cloud cover |
| `dT_corr = dT + f(RH, T_amb)` — humidity-corrected | 1 min | cloud cover, honestly |
| `dT_sigma` | 10–30 min | broken/scattered cloud oscillates |
| `dewpoint_margin = T_amb − T_dew` | 5 min | dew risk on optics **and on our own sensor window** |
| `dP/dt` — pressure trend | 3 h | front approaching |
| `sun_alt`, `moon_alt`, `moon_phase` | computed | see below |

`f(RH, T)` must be **fitted from your own logged data**, not guessed. Collect clear humid nights
and clear dry nights and regress. If you cannot separate them, say so and narrow the claim.

### The sophistication multiplier: local sun/moon ephemeris

Implement solar and lunar position from the RTC plus a hardcoded latitude/longitude, in C, from
standard astronomical algorithms. This is **pure local computation — no API, no network** — and it
transforms the product:

1. **Gating.** Astronomical darkness is `sun_alt < −18°`. Without this the device confidently
   grades a bright evening twilight as "POOR conditions" when the correct answer is "not dark yet."
2. **Attribution.** Knowing moon altitude and phase lets you predict the *expected* moonlight
   contribution and therefore attribute measured brightness to a cause: moon, light pollution, or
   cloud-scattered glow. "Bright because the moon is up and 87% illuminated" is a genuine
   explanation; "bright" is not.
3. **Defensibility.** It is math you wrote and can derive at the whiteboard, which is exactly what
   the individual defense rewards.

This is the single highest-leverage component in the design. It is also self-contained and
testable offline against published almanac values — a perfect unit-test target.

### Classifier: veto gates, not a weighted sum

**CHALLENGE 6: do not use a weighted score.** A weighted sum is hard to explain, hard to defend
line-by-line, and produces absurd outputs (enough darkness "outvoting" solid overcast). Use a
**veto hierarchy**, which is more explainable and trivially traceable:

```
1. NOT_DARK      if sun_alt > -18°                         → state: DAYLIGHT / TWILIGHT
2. UNKNOWN       if any required sensor DEAD or window has
                 < X% expected samples or baseline immature
3. POOR  (veto)  if dT_corr < cloud_overcast_threshold      → "overcast"
4. POOR  (veto)  if dewpoint_margin < 1 °C AND dT collapsed → "likely dew on window, not sky"
5. MARGINAL      if dT_sigma high                           → "broken cloud"
   MARGINAL      if sky_sigma high                          → "unstable brightness"
   MARGINAL      if moon_alt > 0 AND phase > 0.5            → "moonlight limits deep-sky"
6. GOOD          if none of the above fired AND sky_mag
                 within the top band of the site baseline
```

Every rule that fires contributes its reason string. **Explainability is not a feature bolted on;
it is a side effect of the architecture.** That is the right way to build it and a good thing to
say out loud at the defense.

---

## 7. State machine

States: `BOOT` → `DAYLIGHT` / `TWILIGHT` / `UNKNOWN` / `POOR` / `MARGINAL` / `GOOD`, plus
`DEGRADED` (running with a dead sensor) and `FAULT`.

Transition discipline:
- **Minimum dwell time** per state (e.g. 10 min) — prevents flapping.
- **Asymmetric hysteresis.** Promoting toward GOOD requires N consecutive qualifying windows;
  demoting requires fewer. Justify the asymmetry explicitly: a false GOOD sends someone outside
  or on a 40-minute drive for nothing, which is the error that gets the device unplugged. Spec
  Seed 1 makes the same point — *"a monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged."*
- **Every transition is logged** with the rule that caused it and the feature values at the time.
  The transition log is the artifact you will read from at the demo when asked "why did it say
  that at 1 a.m.?"

---

## 8. Data model

Fixed-width binary records — fixed width matters because it makes torn-write detection and
recovery-by-truncation simple.

```c
/* 48 bytes, explicitly padded, little-endian, version-tagged */
struct dsm_record {
    uint64_t t_mono_ns;   /* CLOCK_MONOTONIC — interval math          */
    uint64_t t_real_ns;   /* CLOCK_REALTIME  — wall clock labelling   */
    uint16_t schema_ver;
    uint16_t source_id;   /* which daemon produced this               */
    uint16_t kind;        /* SAMPLE | FEATURE | STATE | HEARTBEAT | FAULT */
    uint16_t flags;       /* VALID | STALE | SYNTHETIC | CALIBRATING  */
    int32_t  v[4];        /* fixed-point payload, scale per kind      */
    uint32_t seq;         /* per-source sequence — proves no gaps     */
    uint32_t crc32;       /* over all preceding bytes                 */
};
```

Design notes worth defending:
- **`seq` per source** gives you drop accounting for free: a gap in sequence numbers is provable
  data loss, and "zero gaps across 48 hours" is a measurable claim.
- **`flags` carries `SYNTHETIC`.** Spec §5 makes this absolute: replayed or synthesized data must
  be labeled *everywhere it appears*. Putting it in the record format means you cannot forget.
- **Fixed-point, not float.** Deterministic across platforms and trivially CRC-able.

---

## 9. Storage architecture (mechanism D)

```
data/
  seg-000001.dsm      append-only segment, rotated at 8 MB or at local noon
  seg-000002.dsm
  index/2026-10-14.rollup    per-night summary written after the night closes
  MANIFEST                   segment list + validated-length watermark
```

- **Superblock** per segment: magic, schema version, creation time, site lat/long.
- **Write batching:** accumulate records in an in-memory buffer, `write()` in one syscall.
- **fsync policy:** `fsync()` every N seconds and on segment rotation. **N is a tunable you will
  experiment on** (§13) — the tradeoff is data-loss window vs. write amplification vs. SD card
  wear. Measuring that curve is real systems work.
- **Recovery:** on startup, read `MANIFEST` watermark, scan forward validating CRCs, truncate at
  the first invalid record, log the truncation. A torn final record is expected and normal, not an
  error condition.
- **Rollups:** after each night, compute per-night summaries (min/median sky_mag, minutes in each
  state, cloud fraction) into a compact index so queries over weeks do not rescan raw segments.
- **Retention:** raw segments age out at a documented horizon; rollups are kept indefinitely.
  Monitor free space and **refuse to write while logging loudly** rather than filling the card.

The crash-consistency story is the deliverable here, and it is testable by literally pulling the
plug — repeatedly, and counting (§13).

---

## 10. Process architecture & mechanism selection

### CHALLENGE 7: pick D + E. Do not pick C or F.

| Mechanism | Fit | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **D** custom crash-consistent storage | Weeks of nightly baseline must survive power cuts; SD wear is real; retrospective queries are a core feature | **Take it.** Strongly justified by the problem. |
| **E** multiprocess + IPC + supervisor | A silently dead sky monitor is this product's nightmare scenario; sensor isolation is a requirement, not garnish | **Take it.** Strongly justified. |
| **A** kernel char driver | Could expose the TSL2591 or MLX90614 via `/dev`. Best resume line in the menu. | **Stretch.** Start it only if M3 lands early. Keep the userspace path as fallback. |
| **B** interrupt vs. polling | Only honest if you switch to the TSL237 pulse-output sensor. The TSL2591's INT pin on a slowly-varying signal is a weak comparison. | **Only with TSL237.** Don't fake it. |
| **C** real-time scheduling | There is no hard deadline in "is the sky dark." Sky brightness changes over minutes. | **Reject.** Forcing `SCHED_FIFO` here is contrived and the defense will find it. |
| **F** no-drop high-rate pipeline | Sampling at 0.1–1 Hz. A "no-drop high-rate pipeline" for a 1 Hz signal is transparently padded. | **Reject.** |

Being able to say *"we considered C and F and rejected them because our sample rates don't justify
them"* is a **stronger** answer at the defense than bolting them on. Judgment is what is being
graded.

### Processes

| Process | Job | Why separate |
|---|---|---|
| `dskyd` | supervisor: fork/exec children, backoff, heartbeat, DEAD marking | must outlive every failure |
| `skyd` | TSL2591 sampling, ~0.2 Hz | an I2C hang here must not kill cloud sensing |
| `cloudd` | MLX90614 sampling, ~1 Hz | the most finicky sensor — isolate it |
| `envd` | BME280 + RTC, ~0.1 Hz | slow, low risk |
| `fusiond` | features, ephemeris, classifier, state machine | the brain; restartable from stored state |
| `stored` | storage layer owner | single writer — avoids multi-writer corruption entirely |
| `dsq` | query CLI (short-lived) | read-only |

**Single-writer storage is a deliberate choice:** exactly one process may write segments, which
eliminates a whole class of concurrency bugs by construction rather than by locking.

---

## 11. IPC design

- **Sensor → hub: POSIX shared-memory ring buffer + semaphore**, one ring per sensor daemon,
  single-producer/single-consumer. Cheap, bounded, and lets the hub detect overrun explicitly
  rather than silently. Per-record `seq` makes any drop provable.
- **Hub → storage: Unix domain socket** (`SOCK_SEQPACKET`). Message-oriented, backpressure comes
  free from the socket buffer, and the fd dying is an immediate, unambiguous signal that the
  storage process is gone.
- **CLI → hub: Unix domain socket** with a small request/response protocol for live state.
- **Supervisor → children: signals + a pipe-based liveness channel.** Each child holds the write
  end of a pipe; the supervisor sees EOF the instant the child dies, without polling. This is a
  clean, classic pattern and a good thing to be able to explain.

Deliberately using **two different IPC mechanisms** is defensible: the sensor path is high-frequency
and fixed-size (shared memory wins), the storage path needs framing and backpressure (sockets win).
Be ready to justify that at the defense rather than saying "we used both to tick a box."

---

## 12. Failure-mode analysis

| # | Failure | Detection | Response | Log evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sensor unplugged | I2C read returns `ENXIO`/`EREMOTEIO` N times consecutively | Mark sensor `DEAD`; fusion drops to `UNKNOWN` or `DEGRADED` with reduced confidence; **never silently substitute a stale value** | `FAULT` record + state transition |
| 2 | **I2C bus lockup** (a real Pi failure mode) | Read timeout; all sensors stop simultaneously | Attempt bus recovery; if it fails, escalate — this is the one fault that can take all sensors at once | `FAULT` with bus state |
| 3 | Sensor stuck (same value forever) | Staleness detector: variance below floor over a long window while others vary | Mark `SUSPECT`, exclude from fusion, keep logging raw | `FAULT` + raw retained |
| 4 | **Dew/frost on the IR window** | `dewpoint_margin < 1 °C` **AND** `dT` collapsed sharply **AND** brightness still dark/stable | Report "likely condensation, not cloud"; enable heater if fitted | dedicated fault class |
| 5 | Process crash | Supervisor sees pipe EOF / `SIGCHLD` | Restart with exponential backoff | restart record with attempt count |
| 6 | **Restart storm** (sensor physically gone, so restarts keep failing) | Backoff exceeds cap / N failures in T | Stop restarting, hold `DEAD`, keep the rest of the system running | explicit "giving up" line |
| 7 | Power cut mid-write | CRC mismatch on the last record at startup | Truncate to last valid record, log it, continue | recovery line with bytes discarded |
| 8 | SD card full | Free-space monitor below threshold | Stop writing raw, keep rollups, log loudly; do not corrupt | pre-emptive warning trail |
| 9 | **RTC battery dead / clock jump** | `CLOCK_REALTIME` moves backwards or disagrees wildly with `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` delta | Keep using monotonic for intervals; flag all affected records; refuse ephemeris-dependent verdicts → `UNKNOWN` | clock-fault record |
| 10 | Slow memory leak | Hourly heartbeat RSS series | Visible as a trend; the soak is the test | heartbeat series (plot it) |

**Failure 4 deserves special attention.** It is the one that is easy to get wrong and it is a
genuinely clever use of fusion: condensation on your own sensor *mimics overcast*, and the only way
to tell them apart is to notice that the other channels disagree. If you build this, it is a strong

# term-project: team rules

Team law for CS 370 (Colorado State University, Prof. Shrideep Pallickara), Fall 2026.
Both partners maintain this file. Claude Code reads it every session, so **a constraint that
lives only in one partner's head protects nothing.**

This file is self-contained on purpose: a teammate who clones only this repo has everything
they need. (Nick has a separate personal course-notes folder one level up; that is not team law
and is not required to work in this repo.)

---

## Project status (update this as things get decided)

- **Idea: LOCKED — Dark Sky Monitor.** An offline device that measures sky brightness and cloud
  cover at one site and grades the night GOOD / MARGINAL / POOR / UNKNOWN with the evidence behind
  the verdict. Full design review in [`docs/design-review.md`](docs/design-review.md).
- **Team:** Nick Marechal + Liam Sagal.
- **Hardware: ORDERED 2026-10-06** — Pi 4 Model B **1 GB** + TSL2591 + MLX90614 (**3.3 V** variant)
  + BME280. See [`docs/bill-of-materials.md`](docs/bill-of-materials.md).
  **Still to buy: USB-C PSU (5.1 V 3 A), microSD, DS3231 RTC, enclosure.** The Pi does not boot
  without the first two.
- **Mechanisms: D** (crash-consistent storage) **+ E** (multiprocess + IPC + supervisor). C and F
  were considered and rejected — at 0.1–1 Hz sampling neither is justified, and being able to say
  why is a stronger defense answer than bolting them on.
- **Next action:** the five-step bring-up checklist in
  [`docs/hardware-log.md`](docs/hardware-log.md) the day the parts land. Step 4 (acrylic vs. LDPE
  film in front of the MLX90614) tests the largest hardware unknown in the project.
- **Open gap:** the problem memo names an archetype, not a named individual. Outreach to the
  Northern Colorado Astronomical Society / CSU astronomy faculty still pending.

## Commands

- Build: `make`            Deploy to Pi: `make deploy PI=pi@<host>`
- Tests: `make test`       Sanitizers: `make asan`      Valgrind: `make memcheck`
- Soak sanity: `make soakcheck` (1-hour miniature of the 48h run)
- **A change is DONE only when build, test, and asan pass. Show the output.**

Targets exist and run today; several are no-ops until there is source to build. Do not let a
target silently become a lie — if it stops doing what its name says, fix it or rename it.

## Hard constraints (graded — spec §3.3, §3.4)

- The PRODUCT makes **no network calls except serving its own LAN interface**. No LLM APIs, no
  cloud inference, no pretrained models, no external weather/data APIs at runtime. The device
  must work with the network cable unplugged. The intelligence in `analysis/` is ours. A grader
  must be able to confirm this in one minute by reading the source tree.
  - Public data (NWS, USGS, etc.) may be used **only** as an offline ground-truth comparison
    while writing the evaluation report — never called from the device's own code.
- Every daemon must be **supervisable**: clean exit codes, no orphaned fds across restart,
  heartbeat within 60s of start.
- Every allocation checked; every syscall's error path handled and logged. The 48-hour soak is
  the test suite of last resort.
- **NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.**
- Replayed or synthesized data is **labeled as such everywhere it appears** — in logs, in the
  report, in the demo. The 48h soak and the live demo run on live sensors.

## Style

- Systems core: **C17, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, no VLAs.** `goto`-cleanup for multi-resource
  functions. ASan/valgrind findings cap that component's score at 50%, so they are bugs, not
  warnings.
- Python permitted only under `tools/` and `ui/`. **No graded mechanism may live there.**
- Smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.

## Ownership

Ownership means **first authorship and answerability at the defense**, not exclusivity. Each
partner is individually examined on their own subsystems plus one question from across the
boundary.

- **Nick:** `src/common/` (record format + CRC — owned by storage, used by everyone) and
  `src/store/` — mechanism **D**, the crash-consistent storage layer.
- **Liam (proposed — Liam to confirm):** `src/super/`, `src/sensors/`, and the IPC — mechanism
  **E**, the supervisor and the sensor daemons. All Linux-only I2C code lives in `src/sensors/`,
  so everything else builds and tests on a Mac.
- **To decide together:** analysis (ephemeris, features, classifier, state machine) and the
  query CLI.
- The agent edits outside the current session owner's area only when told explicitly whose
  session this is.

## Workflow (spec §10, Assignment 0's nine steps apply verbatim)

- Multi-file or algorithmic change: **plan first, wait for approval.** No code in the first pass.
- **Hardware bugs: paste real evidence** — `dmesg`, timing captures, `/proc/interrupts`, logic
  analyzer output. Never propose or accept a fix derived from a verbal description of a sensor
  problem. The agent will confidently reason about a sensor it has never met and be wrong in
  ways only an instrument catches.
- Commit only from a green state; message format `M<n>: <what>`.
- **≥ 40 meaningful commits** across the project, both partners well represented. A pair of
  "final submission" commits is an automatic process grade of **zero, for both partners.**
- Each partner works in **their own clone and their own Claude Code sessions.** Working in one
  shared login defeats the per-partner transcript grading and costs both of you.
- Every milestone's diffs get **two reviews**: a fresh-context agent review and a human review
  by the partner who did not write the code. Each partner's `PROMPTLOG.md` must record at least
  one review of the other's work.

## Transcript discipline (do not skip — spec §6, §10.4)

At **every** milestone M1–M5, each partner copies their raw `.jsonl` sessions from
`~/.claude/projects/<project-dir>/` into `transcripts/<partner>/`. As-is. Not summarized, not
exported, not retyped. See `transcripts/README.md`.

Local transcripts purge after 30 days by default and this project spans more than 30 days.
Losing Week-5 transcripts in Week 15 is a foreseeable loss, and foreseeable losses are not
excused.

  why is a stronger defense answer than bolting them on.
- **Next action:** the five-step bring-up checklist in
  [`docs/hardware-log.md`](docs/hardware-log.md) the day the parts land. Step 4 (acrylic vs. LDPE
  film in front of the MLX90614) tests the largest hardware unknown in the project.
- **Open gap:** the problem memo names an archetype, not a named individual. Outreach to the
  Northern Colorado Astronomical Society / CSU astronomy faculty still pending.

## Commands

- Build: `make`            Deploy to Pi: `make deploy PI=pi@<host>`
- Tests: `make test`       Sanitizers: `make asan`      Valgrind: `make memcheck`
- Soak sanity: `make soakcheck` (1-hour miniature of the 48h run)
- **A change is DONE only when build, test, and asan pass. Show the output.**

Targets exist and run today; several are no-ops until there is source to build. Do not let a
target silently become a lie — if it stops doing what its name says, fix it or rename it.

## Hard constraints (graded — spec §3.3, §3.4)

- The PRODUCT makes **no network calls except serving its own LAN interface**. No LLM APIs, no
  cloud inference, no pretrained models, no external weather/data APIs at runtime. The device
  must work with the network cable unplugged. The intelligence in `analysis/` is ours. A grader
  must be able to confirm this in one minute by reading the source tree.
  - Public data (NWS, USGS, etc.) may be used **only** as an offline ground-truth comparison
    while writing the evaluation report — never called from the device's own code.
- Every daemon must be **supervisable**: clean exit codes, no orphaned fds across restart,
  heartbeat within 60s of start.
- Every allocation checked; every syscall's error path handled and logged. The 48-hour soak is
  the test suite of last resort.
- **NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.**
- Replayed or synthesized data is **labeled as such everywhere it appears** — in logs, in the
  report, in the demo. The 48h soak and the live demo run on live sensors.

## Style

- Systems core: **C17, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, no VLAs.** `goto`-cleanup for multi-resource
  functions. ASan/valgrind findings cap that component's score at 50%, so they are bugs, not
  warnings.
- Python permitted only under `tools/` and `ui/`. **No graded mechanism may live there.**
- Smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.

## Ownership

Ownership means **first authorship and answerability at the defense**, not exclusivity. Each
partner is individually examined on their own subsystems plus one question from across the
boundary.

- **Nick:** `src/common/` (record format + CRC — owned by storage, used by everyone) and
  `src/store/` — mechanism **D**, the crash-consistent storage layer.
- **Liam (proposed — Liam to confirm):** `src/super/`, `src/sensors/`, and the IPC — mechanism
  **E**, the supervisor and the sensor daemons. All Linux-only I2C code lives in `src/sensors/`,
  so everything else builds and tests on a Mac.
- **To decide together:** analysis (ephemeris, features, classifier, state machine) and the
  query CLI.
- The agent edits outside the current session owner's area only when told explicitly whose
  session this is.

## Workflow (spec §10, Assignment 0's nine steps apply verbatim)

- Multi-file or algorithmic change: **plan first, wait for approval.** No code in the first pass.
- **Hardware bugs: paste real evidence** — `dmesg`, timing captures, `/proc/interrupts`, logic
  analyzer output. Never propose or accept a fix derived from a verbal description of a sensor
  problem. The agent will confidently reason about a sensor it has never met and be wrong in
  ways only an instrument catches.
- Commit only from a green state; message format `M<n>: <what>`.
- **≥ 40 meaningful commits** across the project, both partners well represented. A pair of
  "final submission" commits is an automatic process grade of **zero, for both partners.**
- Each partner works in **their own clone and their own Claude Code sessions.** Working in one
  shared login defeats the per-partner transcript grading and costs both of you.
- Every milestone's diffs get **two reviews**: a fresh-context agent review and a human review
  by the partner who did not write the code. Each partner's `PROMPTLOG.md` must record at least
  one review of the other's work.

## Transcript discipline (do not skip — spec §6, §10.4)

At **every** milestone M1–M5, each partner copies their raw `.jsonl` sessions from
`~/.claude/projects/<project-dir>/` into `transcripts/<partner>/`. As-is. Not summarized, not
exported, not retyped. See `transcripts/README.md`.

Local transcripts purge after 30 days by default and this project spans more than 30 days.
Losing Week-5 transcripts in Week 15 is a foreseeable loss, and foreseeable losses are not
excused.

</system-reminder>

197	
198	### CHALLENGE 5: all three sensors share one I2C bus — say so, don't hide it
199	
200	Three separate processes hammering one I2C bus is a genuine design problem, not a free lunch. The
201	Linux I2C subsystem serializes transactions, so you will not get corruption — but you *will* get
202	jitter in sample timing and head-of-line blocking when one sensor is slow. This is an honest
203	tradeoff to state in the design doc and **measure** in the evaluation:
204	
205	- Report per-sensor sample-interval jitter with 1 vs. 3 processes contending.
206	- If jitter proves unacceptable, the fallback is a single `i2cd` broker process owning the bus,
207	  with the three sensor daemons as clients. **Decide this in the design doc, not in week 11.**
208	
209	Do not pretend process isolation is costless. Measuring the cost is worth more than hiding it.
210	
211	---
212	
213	## 6. Sensor-fusion design
214	
215	### The core insight — this is your best paragraph, put it in the memo
216	
217	**A brightness sensor alone is not merely imprecise; it is wrong in a specific, demonstrable,
218	reproducible way.**
219	
220	| Sky brightness | ΔT (ambient − sky) | Reality | A light meter alone says |
221	|---|---|---|---|
222	| Dark | Large (clear) | **Excellent night** | "dark, great" ✅ |
223	| Bright | Large (clear) | Clear but moonlit — planets/doubles yes, deep-sky no | "bright, bad" ❌ *wrong* |
224	| Bright | Small (overcast) | Overcast over a city; cloud reflecting streetlight | "bright, bad" ✅ |
225	| **Dark** | **Small (overcast)** | **Overcast at a dark site — useless** | **"dark, great"** ❌ **catastrophically wrong** |
226	
227	That last row is the whole justification for the second sensor. At a rural dark site an overcast
228	sky is genuinely *darker* than a clear one, because there is no light to reflect. A single-sensor
229	meter confidently recommends the worst possible night. The IR channel catches it, and no
230	if-statement on brightness can.
231	
232	### Features (rolling windows, all locally computed)
233	
234	| Feature | Window | What it discriminates |
235	|---|---|---|
236	| `sky_mag` — brightness, calibrated to relative mag/arcsec² | 1 min | darkness level |
237	| `sky_sigma` — rolling std-dev of brightness | 10–30 min | **passing cloud causes variability, not just a level shift** |
238	| `dT = T_amb − T_sky` | 1 min | cloud cover |
239	| `dT_corr = dT + f(RH, T_amb)` — humidity-corrected | 1 min | cloud cover, honestly |
240	| `dT_sigma` | 10–30 min | broken/scattered cloud oscillates |
241	| `dewpoint_margin = T_amb − T_dew` | 5 min | dew risk on optics **and on our own sensor window** |
242	| `dP/dt` — pressure trend | 3 h | front approaching |
243	| `sun_alt`, `moon_alt`, `moon_phase` | computed | see below |
244	
245	`f(RH, T)` must be **fitted from your own logged data**, not guessed. Collect clear humid nights
246	and clear dry nights and regress. If you cannot separate them, say so and narrow the claim.
247	
248	### The sophistication multiplier: local sun/moon ephemeris
249	
250	Implement solar and lunar position from the RTC plus a hardcoded latitude/longitude, in C, from
251	standard astronomical algorithms. This is **pure local computation — no API, no network** — and it
252	transforms the product:
253	
254	1. **Gating.** Astronomical darkness is `sun_alt < −18°`. Without this the device confidently
255	   grades a bright evening twilight as "POOR conditions" when the correct answer is "not dark yet."
256	2. **Attribution.** Knowing moon altitude and phase lets you predict the *expected* moonlight
257	   contribution and therefore attribute measured brightness to a cause: moon, light pollution, or
258	   cloud-scattered glow. "Bright because the moon is up and 87% illuminated" is a genuine
259	   explanation; "bright" is not.
260	3. **Defensibility.** It is math you wrote and can derive at the whiteboard, which is exactly what
261	   the individual defense rewards.
262	
263	This is the single highest-leverage component in the design. It is also self-contained and
264	testable offline against published almanac values — a perfect unit-test target.
265	
266	### Classifier: veto gates, not a weighted sum
267	
268	**CHALLENGE 6: do not use a weighted score.** A weighted sum is hard to explain, hard to defend
269	line-by-line, and produces absurd outputs (enough darkness "outvoting" solid overcast). Use a
270	**veto hierarchy**, which is more explainable and trivially traceable:
271	
272	```
273	1. NOT_DARK      if sun_alt > -18°                         → state: DAYLIGHT / TWILIGHT
274	2. UNKNOWN       if any required sensor DEAD or window has
275	                 < X% expected samples or baseline immature
276	3. POOR  (veto)  if dT_corr < cloud_overcast_threshold      → "overcast"
277	4. POOR  (veto)  if dewpoint_margin < 1 °C AND dT collapsed → "likely dew on window, not sky"
278	5. MARGINAL      if dT_sigma high                           → "broken cloud"
279	   MARGINAL      if sky_sigma high                          → "unstable brightness"
280	   MARGINAL      if moon_alt > 0 AND phase > 0.5            → "moonlight limits deep-sky"
281	6. GOOD          if none of the above fired AND sky_mag
282	                 within the top band of the site baseline
283	```
284	
285	Every rule that fires contributes its reason string. **Explainability is not a feature bolted on;
286	it is a side effect of the architecture.** That is the right way to build it and a good thing to
287	say out loud at the defense.
288	
289	---
290	
291	## 7. State machine
292	
293	States: `BOOT` → `DAYLIGHT` / `TWILIGHT` / `UNKNOWN` / `POOR` / `MARGINAL` / `GOOD`, plus
294	`DEGRADED` (running with a dead sensor) and `FAULT`.
295	
296	Transition discipline:
297	- **Minimum dwell time** per state (e.g. 10 min) — prevents flapping.
298	- **Asymmetric hysteresis.** Promoting toward GOOD requires N consecutive qualifying windows;
299	  demoting requires fewer. Justify the asymmetry explicitly: a false GOOD sends someone outside
300	  or on a 40-minute drive for nothing, which is the error that gets the device unplugged. Spec
301	  Seed 1 makes the same point — *"a monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged."*
302	- **Every transition is logged** with the rule that caused it and the feature values at the time.
303	  The transition log is the artifact you will read from at the demo when asked "why did it say
304	  that at 1 a.m.?"
305	
306	---
307	
308	## 8. Data model
309	
310	Fixed-width binary records — fixed width matters because it makes torn-write detection and
311	recovery-by-truncation simple.
312	
313	```c
314	/* 48 bytes, explicitly padded, little-endian, version-tagged */
315	struct dsm_record {
316	    uint64_t t_mono_ns;   /* CLOCK_MONOTONIC — interval math          */
317	    uint64_t t_real_ns;   /* CLOCK_REALTIME  — wall clock labelling   */
318	    uint16_t schema_ver;
319	    uint16_t source_id;   /* which daemon produced this               */
320	    uint16_t kind;        /* SAMPLE | FEATURE | STATE | HEARTBEAT | FAULT */
321	    uint16_t flags;       /* VALID | STALE | SYNTHETIC | CALIBRATING  */
322	    int32_t  v[4];        /* fixed-point payload, scale per kind      */
323	    uint32_t seq;         /* per-source sequence — proves no gaps     */
324	    uint32_t crc32;       /* over all preceding bytes                 */
325	};
326	```
327	
328	Design notes worth defending:
329	- **`seq` per source** gives you drop accounting for free: a gap in sequence numbers is provable
330	  data loss, and "zero gaps across 48 hours" is a measurable claim.
331	- **`flags` carries `SYNTHETIC`.** Spec §5 makes this absolute: replayed or synthesized data must
332	  be labeled *everywhere it appears*. Putting it in the record format means you cannot forget.
333	- **Fixed-point, not float.** Deterministic across platforms and trivially CRC-able.
334	
335	---
336	
337	## 9. Storage architecture (mechanism D)
338	
339	```
340	data/
341	  seg-000001.dsm      append-only segment, rotated at 8 MB or at local noon
342	  seg-000002.dsm
343	  index/2026-10-14.rollup    per-night summary written after the night closes
344	  MANIFEST                   segment list + validated-length watermark
345	```
346	
347	- **Superblock** per segment: magic, schema version, creation time, site lat/long.
348	- **Write batching:** accumulate records in an in-memory buffer, `write()` in one syscall.
349	- **fsync policy:** `fsync()` every N seconds and on segment rotation. **N is a tunable you will
350	  experiment on** (§13) — the tradeoff is data-loss window vs. write amplification vs. SD card
351	  wear. Measuring that curve is real systems work.
352	- **Recovery:** on startup, read `MANIFEST` watermark, scan forward validating CRCs, truncate at
353	  the first invalid record, log the truncation. A torn final record is expected and normal, not an
354	  error condition.
355	- **Rollups:** after each night, compute per-night summaries (min/median sky_mag, minutes in each
356	  state, cloud fraction) into a compact index so queries over weeks do not rescan raw segments.
357	- **Retention:** raw segments age out at a documented horizon; rollups are kept indefinitely.
358	  Monitor free space and **refuse to write while logging loudly** rather than filling the card.
359	
360	The crash-consistency story is the deliverable here, and it is testable by literally pulling the
361	plug — repeatedly, and counting (§13).
362	
363	---
364	
365	## 10. Process architecture & mechanism selection
366	
367	### CHALLENGE 7: pick D + E. Do not pick C or F.
368	
369	| Mechanism | Fit | Verdict |
370	|---|---|---|
371	| **D** custom crash-consistent storage | Weeks of nightly baseline must survive power cuts; SD wear is real; retrospective queries are a core feature | **Take it.** Strongly justified by the problem. |
372	| **E** multiprocess + IPC + supervisor | A silently dead sky monitor is this product's nightmare scenario; sensor isolation is a requirement, not garnish | **Take it.** Strongly justified. |
373	| **A** kernel char driver | Could expose the TSL2591 or MLX90614 via `/dev`. Best resume line in the menu. | **Stretch.** Start it only if M3 lands early. Keep the userspace path as fallback. |
374	| **B** interrupt vs. polling | Only honest if you switch to the TSL237 pulse-output sensor. The TSL2591's INT pin on a slowly-varying signal is a weak comparison. | **Only with TSL237.** Don't fake it. |
375	| **C** real-time scheduling | There is no hard deadline in "is the sky dark." Sky brightness changes over minutes. | **Reject.** Forcing `SCHED_FIFO` here is contrived and the defense will find it. |
376	| **F** no-drop high-rate pipeline | Sampling at 0.1–1 Hz. A "no-drop high-rate pipeline" for a 1 Hz signal is transparently padded. | **Reject.** |
377	
378	Being able to say *"we considered C and F and rejected them because our sample rates don't justify
379	them"* is a **stronger** answer at the defense than bolting them on. Judgment is what is being
380	graded.
381	
382	### Processes
383	
384	| Process | Job | Why separate |
385	|---|---|---|
386	| `dskyd` | supervisor: fork/exec children, backoff, heartbeat, DEAD marking | must outlive every failure |
387	| `skyd` | TSL2591 sampling, ~0.2 Hz | an I2C hang here must not kill cloud sensing |
388	| `cloudd` | MLX90614 sampling, ~1 Hz | the most finicky sensor — isolate it |
389	| `envd` | BME280 + RTC, ~0.1 Hz | slow, low risk |
390	| `fusiond` | features, ephemeris, classifier, state machine | the brain; restartable from stored state |
391	| `stored` | storage layer owner | single writer — avoids multi-writer corruption entirely |
392	| `dsq` | query CLI (short-lived) | read-only |
393	
394	**Single-writer storage is a deliberate choice:** exactly one process may write segments, which
395	eliminates a whole class of concurrency bugs by construction rather than by locking.
396	
397	---
398	
399	## 11. IPC design
400	
401	- **Sensor → hub: POSIX shared-memory ring buffer + semaphore**, one ring per sensor daemon,
402	  single-producer/single-consumer. Cheap, bounded, and lets the hub detect overrun explicitly
403	  rather than silently. Per-record `seq` makes any drop provable.
404	- **Hub → storage: Unix domain socket** (`SOCK_SEQPACKET`). Message-oriented, backpressure comes
405	  free from the socket buffer, and the fd dying is an immediate, unambiguous signal that the
406	  storage process is gone.
407	- **CLI → hub: Unix domain socket** with a small request/response protocol for live state.
408	- **Supervisor → children: signals + a pipe-based liveness channel.** Each child holds the write
409	  end of a pipe; the supervisor sees EOF the instant the child dies, without polling. This is a
410	  clean, classic pattern and a good thing to be able to explain.
411	
412	Deliberately using **two different IPC mechanisms** is defensible: the sensor path is high-frequency
413	and fixed-size (shared memory wins), the storage path needs framing and backpressure (sockets win).
414	Be ready to justify that at the defense rather than saying "we used both to tick a box."
415	
416	---
417	
418	## 12. Failure-mode analysis
419	
420	| # | Failure | Detection | Response | Log evidence |
421	|---|---|---|---|---|
422	| 1 | Sensor unplugged | I2C read returns `ENXIO`/`EREMOTEIO` N times consecutively | Mark sensor `DEAD`; fusion drops to `UNKNOWN` or `DEGRADED` with reduced confidence; **never silently substitute a stale value** | `FAULT` record + state transition |
423	| 2 | **I2C bus lockup** (a real Pi failure mode) | Read timeout; all sensors stop simultaneously | Attempt bus recovery; if it fails, escalate — this is the one fault that can take all sensors at once | `FAULT` with bus state |
424	| 3 | Sensor stuck (same value forever) | Staleness detector: variance below floor over a long window while others vary | Mark `SUSPECT`, exclude from fusion, keep logging raw | `FAULT` + raw retained |
425	| 4 | **Dew/frost on the IR window** | `dewpoint_margin < 1 °C` **AND** `dT` collapsed sharply **AND** brightness still dark/stable | Report "likely condensation, not cloud"; enable heater if fitted | dedicated fault class |
426	| 5 | Process crash | Supervisor sees pipe EOF / `SIGCHLD` | Restart with exponential backoff | restart record with attempt count |
427	| 6 | **Restart storm** (sensor physically gone, so restarts keep failing) | Backoff exceeds cap / N failures in T | Stop restarting, hold `DEAD`, keep the rest of the system running | explicit "giving up" line |
428	| 7 | Power cut mid-write | CRC mismatch on the last record at startup | Truncate to last valid record, log it, continue | recovery line with bytes discarded |
429	| 8 | SD card full | Free-space monitor below threshold | Stop writing raw, keep rollups, log loudly; do not corrupt | pre-emptive warning trail |
430	| 9 | **RTC battery dead / clock jump** | `CLOCK_REALTIME` moves backwards or disagrees wildly with `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` delta | Keep using monotonic for intervals; flag all affected records; refuse ephemeris-dependent verdicts → `UNKNOWN` | clock-fault record |
431	| 10 | Slow memory leak | Hourly heartbeat RSS series | Visible as a trend; the soak is the test | heartbeat series (plot it) |
432	
433	**Failure 4 deserves special attention.** It is the one that is easy to get wrong and it is a
434	genuinely clever use of fusion: condensation on your own sensor *mimics overcast*, and the only way
435	to tell them apart is to notice that the other channels disagree. If you build this, it is a strong
436	thing to be asked about.
437	
438	---
439	
440	## 13. Evaluation plan
441	
442	| # | Measurement | Method | Why it matters |

# term-project: team rules

Team law for CS 370 (Colorado State University, Prof. Shrideep Pallickara), Fall 2026.
Both partners maintain this file. Claude Code reads it every session, so **a constraint that
lives only in one partner's head protects nothing.**

This file is self-contained on purpose: a teammate who clones only this repo has everything
they need. (Nick has a separate personal course-notes folder one level up; that is not team law
and is not required to work in this repo.)

---

## Project status (update this as things get decided)

- **Idea: LOCKED — Dark Sky Monitor.** An offline device that measures sky brightness and cloud
  cover at one site and grades the night GOOD / MARGINAL / POOR / UNKNOWN with the evidence behind
  the verdict. Full design review in [`docs/design-review.md`](docs/design-review.md).
- **Team:** Nick Marechal + Liam Sagal.
- **Hardware: ORDERED 2026-10-06** — Pi 4 Model B **1 GB** + TSL2591 + MLX90614 (**3.3 V** variant)
  + BME280. See [`docs/bill-of-materials.md`](docs/bill-of-materials.md).
  **Still to buy: USB-C PSU (5.1 V 3 A), microSD, DS3231 RTC, enclosure.** The Pi does not boot
  without the first two.
- **Mechanisms: D** (crash-consistent storage) **+ E** (multiprocess + IPC + supervisor). C and F
  were considered and rejected — at 0.1–1 Hz sampling neither is justified, and being able to say
  why is a stronger defense answer than bolting them on.
- **Next action:** the five-step bring-up checklist in
  [`docs/hardware-log.md`](docs/hardware-log.md) the day the parts land. Step 4 (acrylic vs. LDPE
  film in front of the MLX90614) tests the largest hardware unknown in the project.
- **Open gap:** the problem memo names an archetype, not a named individual. Outreach to the
  Northern Colorado Astronomical Society / CSU astronomy faculty still pending.

## Commands

- Build: `make`            Deploy to Pi: `make deploy PI=pi@<host>`
- Tests: `make test`       Sanitizers: `make asan`      Valgrind: `make memcheck`
- Soak sanity: `make soakcheck` (1-hour miniature of the 48h run)
- **A change is DONE only when build, test, and asan pass. Show the output.**

Targets exist and run today; several are no-ops until there is source to build. Do not let a
target silently become a lie — if it stops doing what its name says, fix it or rename it.

## Hard constraints (graded — spec §3.3, §3.4)

- The PRODUCT makes **no network calls except serving its own LAN interface**. No LLM APIs, no
  cloud inference, no pretrained models, no external weather/data APIs at runtime. The device
  must work with the network cable unplugged. The intelligence in `analysis/` is ours. A grader
  must be able to confirm this in one minute by reading the source tree.
  - Public data (NWS, USGS, etc.) may be used **only** as an offline ground-truth comparison
    while writing the evaluation report — never called from the device's own code.
- Every daemon must be **supervisable**: clean exit codes, no orphaned fds across restart,
  heartbeat within 60s of start.
- Every allocation checked; every syscall's error path handled and logged. The 48-hour soak is
  the test suite of last resort.
- **NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.**
- Replayed or synthesized data is **labeled as such everywhere it appears** — in logs, in the
  report, in the demo. The 48h soak and the live demo run on live sensors.

## Style

- Systems core: **C17, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, no VLAs.** `goto`-cleanup for multi-resource
  functions. ASan/valgrind findings cap that component's score at 50%, so they are bugs, not
  warnings.

- Smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.

Ownership means **first authorship and answerability at the defense**, not exclusivity. Each
partner is individually examined on their own subsystems plus one question from across the
boundary.

- **Nick:** `src/common/` (record format + CRC — owned by storage, used by everyone) and
  `src/store/` — mechanism **D**, the crash-consistent storage layer.
- **Liam (proposed — Liam to confirm):** `src/super/`, `src/sensors/`, and the IPC — mechanism
  **E**, the supervisor and the sensor daemons. All Linux-only I2C code lives in `src/sensors/`,

  query CLI.

  session this is.

- **Hardware bugs: paste real evidence** — `dmesg`, timing captures, `/proc/interrupts`, logic
  analyzer output. Never propose or accept a fix derived from a verbal description of a sensor
  problem. The agent will confidently reason about a sensor it has never met and be wrong in
  ways only an instrument catches.

Team rule from `CLAUDE.md`, and it exists because the agent will confidently reason about a sensor

`0x60` = BME280 (has humidity). `0x58` = BMP280 (no humidity) → **return the part.**

## 3. MLX90614 sky vs. indoor wall

A clear zenith should read tens of °C below ambient. A wall should read near ambient. If both are
the same, something is in the field of view or the sensor is bad.

Acrylic is expected to be **opaque** in the MLX90614's 8–14 µm band, which would mean a sealed clear

Where the project stands, written so that either partner, or a fresh Claude Code session, can pick
up cold. **Read this after `CLAUDE.md` and before starting work.** Newest entry first. Facts and
evidence only; plans live in `DESIGN.md` and `docs/design-review.md`.

When you finish a chunk of work, add an entry at the top: date, who, what changed, how it was
verified, and what it leaves open.

---

## 2026-10-27 — Pi set up; storage writer done (Nick)

### Milestone position

Canvas dates govern. The spec's estimates (Week 1 = Aug 24) put **M2 at week 7 (~Oct 9)** and
**M3 at week 10 (~Oct 30)**.

| Milestone | Requirement (spec §6) | State |
|---|---|---|
| M0 | Team, hardware ordered, repo + `CLAUDE.md` | Done |
| M1 | Problem memo, transcripts | Done (`PROBLEM.md`; named-user gap recorded in its header) |
| **M2** | `DESIGN.md` (spec §8) | **Not written.** Still the section skeleton. Most of the material exists in `docs/design-review.md` |
| **M2** | Both sensors electrically alive | **Pi ready, sensors not wired yet.** Wiring and bring-up planned for the evening of 2026-10-27 |
| **M2** | Transcripts copied out | **Not done for M2** (only `transcripts/*/2026-09-23-m0-m1/` exist) |
| M3 | Both sensors through the real pipeline into real storage; one menu mechanism working | Storage writer exists (below); no sensor code, pipeline, or supervisor yet |

Commit count: **16** (Nick 15, Liam 1). The spec requires ≥ 40 meaningful commits across the
project with both partners well represented.

### Hardware

All parts arrived 2026-10-13. The Pi was set up headless on 2026-10-27. Full detail and raw output
are in [`hardware-log.md`](hardware-log.md) §0.

- Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit. Hostname `darksky`, reached as `darksky.local` from the same Wi-Fi.
  Nick's Pi, Nick's login.
- Installed: `git build-essential i2c-tools valgrind rsync`. I2C is on (`/dev/i2c-1` exists).
- Power: `vcgencmd get_throttled` → `0x0`.
- First Linux build of the project: `make test` 15/0, `make memcheck` 0 errors, no leaks.
- **Not done yet:** sensor wiring, `i2cdetect`, BME280 chip ID, and the rest of the bring-up
  checklist in `hardware-log.md` §1–5.
- **No RTC** (DS3231 deferred). The Pi gets the real time from the network at boot. Without a
  network, `CLOCK_REALTIME` is wrong after a power cut, and so is anything that depends on it
  (`t_real_ns`, and later the sun/moon calculations).

### Code that exists

Everything below builds with `-std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror` and passes `make test` and
`make asan` on macOS. Steps 0–2 also pass `make memcheck` on the Pi.

| File | What it is | Owner (CLAUDE.md map) |
|---|---|---|
| `Makefile` | One test binary `build/test_all`; targets `test`, `asan`, `memcheck`, `deploy`, `clean`, `help`. `-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L` is required for glibc to declare `fsync`, `pread`, `clock_gettime`, etc. under `-std=c17` | shared |
| `tests/check.h`, `tests/test_main.c`, `tests/suites.h` | `CHECK(cond, fmt, ...)` counts and prints failures; `main` runs every suite and exits non-zero on any failure | shared |
| `src/common/crc32.{c,h}` | `dsm_crc32(data, len)`: CRC-32/IEEE, bit-at-a-time. Tested against the published check value `0xCBF43926` | Nick |
| `src/common/record.{c,h}` | `struct dsm_record`: **the 48-byte format every process shares** (see the contract below) | Nick |
| `src/store/store.{c,h}` | Append-only store file: a 24-byte header, then records back to back | Nick |

Tests: 116 checks across `tests/test_crc32.c`, `tests/test_record.c`, `tests/test_store.c`.

### The record contract (`src/common/record.h`)

Everything that produces data produces `struct dsm_record`. The rules:

1. `record_init(&r, kind, source_id)` first. It zeroes all 48 bytes. Uninitialized bytes would be
   fed into the CRC, which valgrind reports.
2. Fill in the fields.
3. `record_seal(&r)` **last**. Any change after sealing makes `record_intact()` false.
4. `seq` counts per source, starting at 0, +1 per record. A gap is provable lost data.
5. `t_mono_ns` = `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (for intervals); `t_real_ns` = `CLOCK_REALTIME` (wall-clock
   label).
6. Replayed or simulated data **must** set `DSM_FLAG_SYNTHETIC` (spec §5).
7. Values in `v[0..3]` are integers (fixed-point), never floats.

**The store refuses any record that isn't sealed** (`STORE_ERR_BADREC`). That's deliberate. Crash
recovery will cut a file off at its first bad record, so letting one unsealed record in would cost
every good record written after it.

### Proposed sample payload (NOT agreed — both partners to decide)

Which `source_id` each sensor uses, and what goes in each `v[]` slot, is a cross-boundary
interface. Nothing depends on it yet. This is only a starting proposal:

| `source_id` | Process / sensor | `v[0]` | `v[1]` | `v[2]` | `v[3]` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | *(reserved: a zeroed record must never look real)* | | | | |
| 1 | `skyd` / TSL2591 | CH0 raw count (full spectrum) | CH1 raw count (IR) | gain multiplier (1, 25, 428, 9876) | integration time, ms |
| 2 | `cloudd` / MLX90614 | sky (object) temp, m°C | sensor (ambient) temp, m°C | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | `envd` / BME280 | temperature, m°C | humidity, milli-%RH | pressure, Pa | 0 |

The reasoning behind it:

- **Raw TSL2591 counts rather than lux.** Lux isn't meaningful at night-sky levels, and the
  design converts brightness to relative mag/arcsec² as a *feature* later (`design-review.md` §6).
  Storing raw counts plus gain and integration time means that conversion can be redone from old
  data.
- **The MLX90614 reports in steps of 0.02 K**, which is exactly 20 m°C, so milli-degrees store it
  with no rounding: `m°C = raw * 20 - 273150`.

Still open: how a failed read is recorded (a `FAULT` record, or a `SAMPLE` without
`DSM_FLAG_VALID`), and the `source_id`s for `fusiond` and the supervisor.

### Store API (`src/store/store.h`) as of today

```c
enum store_status store_open(const char *path, struct dsm_store **out);   /* create or reopen */
enum store_status store_append(struct dsm_store *s, const struct dsm_record *r);
enum store_status store_close(struct dsm_store *s);                         /* NULL-safe */
```

Status values: `STORE_OK`, `STORE_ERR_IO` (check `errno`), `STORE_ERR_FORMAT` (an existing file
that isn't ours; refused, left untouched), `STORE_ERR_BADREC` (unsealed record; nothing written),
`STORE_ERR_BROKEN` (an earlier write failed; no more appends on this handle).

What it guarantees **today**, and what it doesn't:

- ✅ New file gets a header: magic `DSKY`, schema version, record size, creation time, CRC.
  Reopening appends at the end and never rewrites the header.
- ✅ Wrong magic, schema, or record size, a damaged header, or a file shorter than a header →
  refused, and the file is left untouched.
- ✅ After a failed or partial write, the handle refuses all further appends, so nothing gets
  written out of line with the 48-byte slots. Tested by lowering `RLIMIT_FSIZE` to make a real
  `write()` fail.
- ✅ The fd is `O_CLOEXEC`, so it isn't inherited across `exec` by supervised children.
- ❌ **No `fsync` yet.** A power cut can lose records the kernel hasn't written to the card yet.
- ❌ **No recovery yet.** If a crash leaves a partial record at the end, reopening appends after
  it, out of line. The recovery step fixes this.
- ❌ One writer per file is assumed. The design gives storage a single writer process (`stored`).
- Open question for recovery: a file of 1–23 bytes is refused today. It could be a crash during
  header creation (ours) or a stranger's file, and there's no way to tell them apart.

**Remaining storage steps:** (4) recovery: scan, validate each CRC, truncate at the first bad
record, report what was discarded; (5) write batching + `fsync` policy, with counters for the
fsync experiment. After those: segment rotation, `MANIFEST`, nightly rollups, free-space guard,
the `dsq` query CLI.

### Building and running on the Pi

- From a Mac or Linux clone: `make deploy PI=<user>@<host>` (rsync; copies changed files, skips
  `.git`, `build`, `transcripts`), then on the Pi `cd ~/term-project && make test && make memcheck`.
- `valgrind` only runs on Linux. The Pi or a CS department machine is where `make memcheck` means
  something.
- **Linux-only code needs a Makefile split that doesn't exist yet.** The Makefile currently builds
  every file in `SRC` on every machine, and one partner develops on macOS. Code that includes
  `<linux/i2c-dev.h>` or calls `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` would break the Mac build if it went straight
  into `SRC`. Keeping it in `src/sensors/` (per `CLAUDE.md`) and adding it through a Linux-only
  variable (e.g. `ifeq ($(shell uname -s),Linux)`) keeps `make test` working everywhere.

### Open work for M2 (none of it is started)

**1. `DESIGN.md`** (10 pts, team). Spec §8: architecture with rates on every arrow, mechanism
mapping justified from the user's requirements, failure-mode table, storage and data,
constraints and substitutions, evaluation plan, ownership map, AI-use plan. Sources:
`design-review.md` §5 (architecture), §8–9 (data, storage), §10–11 (processes, IPC), §12
(failure modes), §13 (evaluation).

**2. Sensors electrically alive.** Evidence goes in `hardware-log.md` §1–5: `i2cdetect -y 1`
should show `0x29`, `0x5A`, `0x76`/`0x77`. BME280 chip ID first, since it has a return window.

**3. Sensor-reading code, `src/sensors/`** (the CLAUDE.md ownership map lists this area under
mechanism E). Nothing exists. A natural split that can be built and tested without hardware:

- **Pure conversion functions:** register bytes in, fixed-point units out (the proposed payload
  above). No I/O, so they build anywhere. Unit-test them with the worked examples in the
  datasheets.
- **A thin Linux I2C layer:** `open("/dev/i2c-1")` + `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` with a combined
  write-then-read (repeated start). Linux-only, see the Makefile note above.
- **A one-shot check program** that reads all three sensors once and prints values. This is the
  M2 "electrically alive" evidence, and it becomes the core of `skyd` / `cloudd` / `envd` at M3.

**Register facts to start from. Verify every one against the datasheet PDF before relying on
it. The team rule is evidence over recall, and these came from recall.**

| Sensor | Address | Identity check | Key registers / protocol | Gotchas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BME280 | `0x76` (or `0x77`) | `0xD0` → `0x60`. `0x58` means a BMP280 (no humidity) | Calibration `0x88–0xA1` and `0xE1–0xE7`; `ctrl_hum 0xF2`, `ctrl_meas 0xF4`, `config 0xF5`; data burst `0xF7–0xFE` (P, T, H). Forced mode: write `ctrl_meas` with mode `01`, wait, read | Write `ctrl_hum` **before** `ctrl_meas` or the humidity setting is ignored. Use the datasheet's integer compensation code (32-bit T and H, 64-bit P); temperature must be computed first because P and H use its `t_fine` |
| TSL2591 | `0x29` | ID register `0x12` → `0x50` | Every register access goes through the command byte `0xA0 \| reg`. `ENABLE 0x00` (PON + AEN = `0x03`), `CONTROL 0x01` (gain bits 5:4, integration time bits 2:0: 100–600 ms), `STATUS 0x13` (AVALID bit 0), CH0 `0x14–0x15`, CH1 `0x16–0x17`, little-endian | At max gain indoors it saturates. The dark offset (hardware-log §5) is the noise floor every night reading sits on |
| MLX90614 | `0x5A` | — | SMBus read-word from RAM: `0x06` = ambient, `0x07` = object. Returns 3 bytes: LSB, MSB, PEC. `°C = raw × 0.02 − 273.15` | Needs a **repeated start** (combined write-read). PEC is CRC-8 (poly `0x07`) over addr+W, command, addr+R, LSB, MSB: check it. MSB bit 7 set on an object reading = error flag. Known Pi problem with this chip's clock stretching: lower `i2c_arm_baudrate` or use `i2c-gpio` (design-review §3) |

**4. Supervisor + IPC (mechanism E)** — not needed for M2, needed for M3. `design-review.md`
§10–11: `dskyd` fork/execs the children, sees each death through pipe EOF / `SIGCHLD`, restarts with
exponential backoff, and gives up with a logged `DEAD` state on a restart storm. Can be built and
tested on any Linux machine with stand-in child processes; no sensors needed.

**5. Process items for M2.** Each partner copies out their `.jsonl` transcripts to
`transcripts/<name>/<date>-m2/`. Each partner's `PROMPTLOG` needs, at some point, a review of
the *other* partner's code. `src/store/` and `src/common/` are reviewable now. The ownership map's
"proposed" side still needs confirming in `CLAUDE.md`.
